# **NFS 4 High Stakes file specs** #

*Last time updated: 2026-10-29 13:06:40.096825+00:00*

*Generated by [TailsLab](../README.md) from its parser code.*


# **Info by file extensions** #

**Data/Audio/MUSIC/\*.ASF** song: `GAME*` in race, `MENU*`, `GARAGE1`, `SHOW`, `CREDITS`. [EaAudioStreams](#eaaudiostreams)

**\*.BNK** sound bank. [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)

**Data/Tracks/\<track\>/Tr\<nn\>.can**, **Tr00a.can** animation path of knocked-away objects. [Nfs3CanAnimation](#nfs3cananimation)

**Data/Cars/\<car\>/car.viv: carp.txt** (**carp\<n\>.txt**) car physics, plain text (label and value lines). [Nfs4CarPhysics](#nfs4carphysics). The converter writes it as `carp.txt.json` (named values) and `carp.txt.bin` (the file as it is)

**\*.FCE** 3D model (car.fce in car.viv: car model). [Fce4Geometry](#fce4geometry)

**\*.FFN** bitmap font. [FfnFont](#ffnfont)

**\*.FRD** main track file. [Nfs4FrdMap](#nfs4frdmap)

**Data/Tracks/\<track\>/heights.sim** ceiling heights of the track slices. [Nfs4HeightsSim](#nfs4heightssim)

**Data/Tracks/\<track\>/spdFA.bin**, **spdRA.bin** AI line (speeds, lanes, lateral offsets) of the track slices, forward / reversed. [Nfs4SpeedFile](#nfs4speedfile)

**Data/Tracks/\<track\>/Tr.ini** track settings (`TrN.ini` night, `TrW.ini` weather, `TrNW.ini` both): sky, clouds, fog, sun, light, glows. [Nfs4TrackIni](#nfs4trackini). The converter writes the sky sphere texture `spherical.png` next to the PNGs of `sky.qfs` from its horizon strips `HDC0`..`HDC7`, clouds `CLDD`, sun `SUND` and `Tr.ini`

**\*.FSH** image archive. [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock)

**\*.QFS** image archive. [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock), [compressed](eac_compressions.md)

**\*.VIV** archive with some data. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

Did not find what you need or some given data is wrong? Please submit an
[issue](https://github.com/AndyGura/nfs-resources-converter/issues/new)

## **Archives** ##
### **ShpiBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A container of images and palettes for them ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SHPI" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this SHPI block in bytes |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **shpi_dir** | 4 | UTF-8 string | One of: "LN32", "GIMX", "WRAP". The purpose is unknown |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*8 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: 8-bytes record, first 4 bytes is a UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian) | An array of items, each of them represents name of SHPI item (image or palette) and offset to item data in file, relatively to SHPI block start (where resource id string is presented). Names are not always unique |
| 16 + num_items\*8 | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*8 + up to the first item offset | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets to some of the entries are defined in `items_descr` block. Between them there can be non-indexed entries (palettes and texts). Possible item types:<br/>- [EacImage](#eacimage)<br/>- [EacPalette](#eacpalette) |
### **BigfBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A block-container with various data: image archives, GEO geometries, sound banks, other BIGF blocks... ####

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BIGF" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The length of this BIGF block in bytes. NFS6 stores the length without padding between items: header plus item lengths |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |

| 16 + num_items\*9..? | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*9 + up to the first item offset..? | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets and lengths are defined in previous block. Possible item types:<br/>- [Fce4Geometry](#fce4geometry)<br/>- [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock), can be compressed like QFS file<br/>- [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)<br/>- [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)<br/>- pure TGA image |

### **EaSoundBank** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound bank "BNKl" (*.BNK of NFS2, NFS2 SE, NFS3, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6): a table of sound patches, then their wave data. Car banks (NFS2 `<car>.BNK` / `O<car>.BNK` (opponent) / `S<car>.BNK`, NFS3 `car.bnk` / `ocar.bnk` / `scar.bnk` in car.viv, NFS4 `careng.bnk` / `ocareng.bnk` / `scareng.bnk`, NFS3/NFS4 `GENCAR.BNK`, traffic `TRUCK.BNK`...) use indices 0 and 1 for the engine (looped), 2 for a one-shot with random detune range 200-250 (gear shift, like `gear` of TNFS car banks) and 3 for the horn (looped). Opponent banks have the engine and the horn only: NFS2 `O<car>.BNK` in slots 0 and 1 of a 2-slot table, NFS3 `ocar.bnk` / NFS4 `ocareng.bnk` in slots 0 and 3. NFS4 `careng.bnk` has more engine samples at higher indices (presumably one per RPM range). `W*.BNK` of NFS2 SE are car speech ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BNKl" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 2 (NFS2, NFS2 SE, most of NFS3 GameData/Audio/SFX), 4 (NFS3 car.viv, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6) or 5 (NFS6) |
| 6 | **num_items** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of slots in `items_descr` |
| 8 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 2 and 4: offset of the wave data, i.e. the length of the table and the patches. Version 5: file length |
| 12 | **wave_data_length** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 4: length of the wave data. Version 5: 0 |
| 12..16 | **unk0** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 12..20 | **items_descr** | num_items\*4 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of every patch, relative to its own position in this table, the array index being the sample index used by the game. 0 is an empty slot |
| 12 + num_items\*4..20 + num_items\*4 | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | Sound patches ([EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch)) at the offsets of `items_descr`, then wave data |
## **Geometries** ##
### **Fce4Geometry** ###
#### **Size**: 8248..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: FCE 3D model, version 4 (NFS4: High Stakes, Motor City Online). Used for cars (car.fce in car.viv), dashboards (dash.fce), police officers, helicopter, menu models. Consists of up to 64 parts, each of them is a separate mesh with own position, and up to 16 "dummies": named points, which are used for lights, license plates, smoke and water effects. In addition to FCE3, every vertex has a "damaged" position, used when car is crashed. Coordinate system: X points right, Y up, Z forward. The unit is meter. Texture is a TGA image car00.tga, which is located next to car.fce in car.viv. Alpha channel of the texture defines which car color is applied to the pixel: 224 primary, 164 interior, 96 secondary, 32 driver hair color ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **version** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Format version. 0x00101014 in NFS4, 0x00101015 in Motor City Online (FCE4M) |
| 4 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **num_triangles** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of triangles in the model |
| 12 | **num_vertices** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of vertices in the model |
| 16 | **num_arts** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of "arts" (texture pages?). 1, unless triangles use non-zero `tex_page` |
| 20 | **vertices_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of vertices table, relative to header end (0x2038). Tables go one after another in order: vertices, normals, triangles, reserved areas 1-3, undamaged vertices, undamaged normals, damaged vertices, damaged normals, reserved area 4, animation flags, reserved areas 5-6 |
| 24 | **normals_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of normals table, relative to header end |
| 28 | **triangles_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of triangles table, relative to header end |
| 32 | **reserve1_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of reserved area 1, relative to header end |
| 36 | **reserve2_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of reserved area 2, relative to header end |
| 40 | **reserve3_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of reserved area 3, relative to header end |

| 56 | **damaged_normals_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of damaged normals table, relative to header end |

| 76 | **half_size** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Half-size of the whole model (bounding box) along x (right), y (up), z (forward), at header +0x4c: nfs4.exe uses it as the half extents of the car's rigid body box (Car_Reset 0x4448d0 copies it into the game setup car and passes it to the body setup 0x4f4a20; human players take the front end's copy, the FCE's with game setup flag 2). Half the extent of the parts' vertices in 34 of the 41 NFS4 car models (the others within a few cm). The gg-web-engine export writes it as it is, in these axes, to `collisionHalfSize` of the `.meta` (the GLB has y and z swapped: x right, y forward, z up) |

| 2276 | **driver_hair_colors** | 64 | Array of `16` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: Car color in HSB. Every component is 0..255: hue = degrees / 360 * 255, saturation = percent / 100 * 255, brightness = percent / 100 * 255 | Driver hair colors. Only first `num_colors` are used |
| 2340 | **unk1** | 260 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 2600 | **dummy_names** | 1024 | Array of `16` items<br/>Item size: 64 bytes<br/>Item type: UTF-8 string | Names of dummies. The name defines what the dummy is. Special names: ":LICENSE", ":LICMED", ":LICLOW" (license plate in high/medium/low LOD), ":LICENSE_EURO" (long license plate), ":SMOKE" (smoke when shifting gears), ":WATER" (water generator). Other dummies are lights, where every letter is a property: 1st is kind ("H": headlight, "T": taillight, "B": brake light, "R": reverse light, "P": direction indicator, "S": siren), 2nd is color ("W": white, "R": red, "B": blue, "O": orange, "Y": yellow), 3rd is "Y"/"N" for breakable or not, 4th is flashing mode ("O"/"E" for odd/even flashing, "N" for no flashing), 5th is intensity 0..9, 6th and 7th are flashing time and delay 0..9 |

### **Fce4Triangle** ###
#### **Size**: 56 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A single triangle of FCE4 mesh ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **tex_page** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Texture page index. 0 for car models (texture car00.tga), other values are used by multi-texture models like police officers and pursuit road objects |
| 4 | **vertex_indices** | 12 | Array of `3` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Vertex indices, local to the part: add `part_first_vertex` of the part to get index in `vertices` |
| 16 | **unk0** | 12 | Array of `3` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 28 | **flags** | 4 | 32 flags container<br/><details><summary>flag names (from least to most significant)</summary>0: matte<br/>1: high_chrome<br/>2: no_cull<br/>3: semi_transparent<br/>5: window<br/>6: front_window<br/>7: left_window<br/>8: back_window<br/>9: right_window<br/>10: broken_window</details> | Triangle flags. "matte": no environment reflection (underbody), "high_chrome": strong reflection (windows), "no_cull": triangle is visible from both sides, "semi_transparent": translucent triangle (windows). Triangle is visible behind a semi-transparent triangle only if it has smaller index. "window" is set for all car windows, together with one of "front_window", "left_window", "back_window", "right_window". "broken_window" marks a texture of broken glass, which replaces the window after crash |
| 32 | **u** | 12 | Array of `3` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: Float number (little-endian) | Texture U coordinates of 3 vertices, 0..1 |
| 44 | **v** | 12 | Array of `3` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: Float number (little-endian) | Texture V coordinates of 3 vertices, 0..1, from top to bottom |
### **Fce4Color** ###
#### **Size**: 4 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Car color in HSB. Every component is 0..255: hue = degrees / 360 * 255, saturation = percent / 100 * 255, brightness = percent / 100 * 255 ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **hue** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Hue |
| 1 | **saturation** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Saturation |
| 2 | **brightness** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Brightness |
| 3 | **transparency** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Transparency |
## **Maps** ##
### **Nfs4FrdMap** ###
#### **Size**: 44..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Main track file (NFS4 High Stakes). The track is split into blocks (segments): block headers with all counts come first, then block bodies with vertices, polygons at 3 levels of detail and objects. Polygon textures index the track QFS archive (<track>0.QFS), skipping its mirrored texture copies; UV-s are not stored, texture orientation is defined by polygon flags ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **unk** | 28 | Bytes | Unknown header, not read by nfs4.exe (the FRD loader 0x4327b0 reads only `num_blocks` and `num_vroad` of the first 36 bytes) |
| 28 | **num_blocks** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of the last track block: the number of blocks - 1 |
| 32 | **num_vroad** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of virtual road records: the number of track slices |
| 36 | **vroad** | num_vroad\*84 | Array of `num_vroad` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs4VRoadBlock](#nfs4vroadblock) | Virtual road: one record per track slice, 8 slices per block (`num_slices` of the block headers). heights.sim, spdFA.bin and spdRA.bin have one value per record |
| 36 + num_vroad\*84 | **blocks_headers** | (num_blocks+1)\*1512 | Array of `num_blocks+1` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs4TrkBlockHeader](#nfs4trkblockheader) | Metadata for every track block, incl. the counts used to size the corresponding entry of `blocks` |
| 36 + num_vroad\*84 + (num_blocks+1)\*1512 | **blocks** | (num_blocks+1)\*0..? | Array of `num_blocks+1` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs4TrkBlock](#nfs4trkblock) | Track block geometry and extra data |
| 36 + num_vroad\*84 + (num_blocks+1)\*1512 + (num_blocks+1)\*0..? | **num_global_objects_0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of objects in `global_objects_0` |
| 40 + num_vroad\*84 + (num_blocks+1)\*1512 + (num_blocks+1)\*0..? | **global_objects_0** | 0..? | A group of extra (out-of-terrain) objects: e.g. billboards, animated objects, physics props | Extra objects not attached to any track block |

### **Nfs4VRoadBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 84 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Virtual road record of a track slice: the slice centre on the road with the road frame, distances to the road edges, lanes and side types. One per slice, 8 slices per track block: block b has the slices b * 8 .. b * 8 + `num_slices` - 1 of its header (nfs4.exe 0x439d60). nfs4.exe reads these records in place from the loaded file (0x64f1a4); NFS4 has no COL file, this is its `collision_data` ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **ref_point** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | The slice centre on the road (nfs4.exe 0x4f63d0, 0x4395f0): the road frame origin, the point a car is placed from (0x4f4590) |
| 12 | **normal** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Road normal (up), row 1 of the road frame (0x4395f0, 0x4f63d0) |
| 24 | **forward** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Road forward vector, row 2 of the road frame (0x4395f0, 0x4f4590) |
| 36 | **right** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Road right vector, row 0 of the road frame. A point p is left of the centre when right . (p - ref_point) <= 0 (nfs4.exe 0x4399d0, the wall type choice of 0x45cf20) |
| 48 | **left_wall** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Distance from the slice centre to the left wall/edge in meters: the lateral offset of an AI lane is kept at least a margin (2 m for the AI line the game makes when the speed file is short) inside it (nfs4.exe 0x41e0d0) |
| 52 | **right_wall** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Distance from the slice centre to the right wall/edge in meters, as `left_wall` |
| 56 | **left_lane_width** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Width of the lanes left of the centre in meters (0..10 in the NFS4 tracks). Lane centres: -i x width - width / 2 (nfs4.exe 0x448c20, the car reset), the grid (0x444700); a lateral offset < 0 is lane 6 + round((width / 2 + offset) / width) (0x41cce0) |
| 60 | **right_lane_width** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Width of the lanes right of the centre in meters (2..10): lane centres i x width + width / 2 (0x448c20, 0x444700), offset >= 0 is lane 7 + round((offset - width / 2) / width) (0x41cce0) |
| 64 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 0xFFFFFFFF in nearly all records of the NFS4 tracks |
| 68 | **left_lanes** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Number of lanes left of the centre (0..4): the car reset tries their centres for a free spot (nfs4.exe 0x448c20). AI lane 6 - this, the first past them, is an edge lane for 0x41e0d0 (its offset is the boundary of the outer lane minus the margin instead of a lane centre) |
| 72 | **right_lanes** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Number of lanes right of the centre (1..4), as `left_lanes` (0x448c20); AI lane 7 + this is the edge lane on the right (0x41e0d0) |
| 76 | **lane_open_bits** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Usable lanes: lane i (0..13, 6 and 7 the lanes either side of the centre, see `left_lane_width`) is open when bit 15 - clamp(i + 1, 0, 15) is set (nfs4.exe 0x41cc00); a car is reset only onto an open lane (0x448870). 0x3c0 (lanes 5..8) the most common |
| 80 | **left_side_type** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Type of the road side left of the centre (0..5). Two code-verified uses of this byte: 2 = covered (tunnel, roof: no weather there, the ceiling of heights.sim applies; nfs4.exe 0x4399d0 / 0x439ab0, with polygon surface bit 0x20); and the wall crash type of a wall hit on this side, crash type 0x40000 | value, 0 or above 7 counting as 4 (0x45cf20) |
| 81 | **right_side_type** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Type of the road side right of the centre, as `left_side_type` (0x4399d0, 0x45cf20) |
| 82 | **unk1** | 2 | Array of `2` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Values 0..5, often equal to each other |

### **Nfs4TrkBlockHeader** ###
#### **Size**: 1512 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Metadata of a track block (segment of the track): position, bounds, neighbours and the counts which define sizes of all arrays in the [Nfs4TrkBlock](#nfs4trkblock) with the same index. nfs4.exe copies the 0x5e8 bytes as they are (0x4327b0, 300 blocks at most) and writes the addresses of the block arrays into the pointer slots ####

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **polygon_chunk_sizes** | 44 | Array of `11` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of polygons in each of the 11 polygon chunks (see Nfs4TrkBlock) of this block. Chunk 4 (high-res track) holds the road polygons of the track position search (nfs4.exe 0x439fe0) |
| 44 | **polygon_chunk_pointers** | 44 | Array of `11` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slots: the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4327b0) writes each polygon chunk's address here, 0 for an empty chunk. The files hold leftovers of the tool's memory |
| 88 | **num_vertices** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Total amount of vertices stored for this block |
| 92 | **num_vertices_high** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of vertices used by high-res terrain polygons |
| 96 | **num_vertices_low** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of vertices used by low-res terrain polygons |
| 100 | **num_vertices_med** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of vertices used by medium-res terrain polygons |
| 104 | **num_vertices_dup** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Equals to `num_vertices` |
| 108 | **num_vertices_obj** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of vertices used by per-block objects? |
| 112 | **vertex_pointers** | 8 | Array of `2` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slots of `vertices` and `vertex_shading`, written by the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4327b0); leftovers in the files |
| 120 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Position of the block in the world: a point on the road at the block start. Positions of all blocks form the track path |
| 132 | **bounds** | 48 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Block bounding rectangle |
| 180 | **neighbour_data** | 1200 | Array of `300` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs4NeighbourData](#nfs4neighbourdata) | Neighbouring blocks. Unused items have block index -1 |
| 1380 | **object_chunk_counts** | 32 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs4BlockCount](#nfs4blockcount) | Amount of extra objects in each of the 4 per-block extra object chunks (see Nfs4TrkBlock) |
| 1412 | **num_polygons** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of items in `polygon_vroad_data` (0x18-byte polygon records, nfs4.exe block +0x584) |
| 1416 | **bounds_min** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Minimum corner of the axis-aligned bounding box of the block. Its x / z range is the block test of the track position search and the span of the polygon records' cells (nfs4.exe 0x439fe0); also the box centre of the nearest block (0x439ea0) |
| 1428 | **bounds_max** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Maximum corner of the axis-aligned bounding box of the block, see `bounds_min` |
| 1440 | **polygon_vroad_data_pointer** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slot of `polygon_vroad_data`, written by the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4327b0); leftovers in the files |
| 1444 | **num_slices** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of track slices (`vroad` records) of the block: 8, the last block fewer. Block b owns the vroad records b * 8 .. b * 8 + this - 1 (nfs4.exe 0x439d60); the sum over all blocks is `num_vroad` |
| 1448 | **num_xobj** | 8 | [Nfs4BlockCount](#nfs4blockcount) | Amount of items in `xobj` |
| 1456 | **num_polyobj** | 8 | [Nfs4BlockCount](#nfs4blockcount) | Amount of items in `xobj2` |
| 1464 | **num_soundsrc** | 8 | [Nfs4BlockCount](#nfs4blockcount) | Amount of items in `soundsrc` |
| 1472 | **num_lightsrc** | 8 | [Nfs4BlockCount](#nfs4blockcount) | Amount of items in `lightsrc` |
| 1480 | **neighbors** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Neighbouring block numbers, -1 unused (4 to 6 of them in the NFS4 tracks): a block is near another when it is that block or one of its 8 neighbours (nfs4.exe 0x4392d0: the wall test of the car collisions, 0x45cde0) |
### **Nfs4PolygonVroadData** ###
#### **Size**: 24 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Road data of a high-res track polygon (chunk 4) of the block, 0x18 bytes: where the polygon lies in the block's cell grid, its wall edges and surface, its normal and forward vectors. nfs4.exe's track position search (0x439fe0) scans these records for the one whose cell range holds the point and whose polygon holds it ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **cell_z_min** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Lowest z cell of the polygon: the x / z box of the block (`bounds_min` .. `bounds_max` of its header) is split into 256 cells per axis, cell = trunc((p - min) x 255 / (max - min)) (nfs4.exe 0x439fe0) |
| 1 | **cell_z_max** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Highest z cell of the polygon |
| 2 | **cell_x_min** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Lowest x cell of the polygon |
| 3 | **cell_x_max** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Highest x cell of the polygon |
| 4 | **edge_walls** | 4 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Wall flag of each polygon edge: corners 0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-0 (edge bits 1, 2, 4, 8 of nfs4.exe 0x4393e0). 0 or 255 (rarely 1) in the NFS4 tracks. A car box point beyond the edges of its polygon is pushed back by the mean of the normals of those edges whose flag is not 0 (the road edge walls, 0x45cf20, on polygons with `surface.walls`) |
| 8 | **surface** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>1-bit flag "walls"<br/>1-bit flag "objects"<br/>1-bit flag "covered"<br/>5-bits int "surface_type" | Surface byte: bits 0x1f `surface_type` (the grip table index of nfs4.exe 0x5c0820, 0 and 0xe not drivable: 0x45cde0, 0x4f3e40), bit 0x20 `covered` (0x439ab0), bit 0x40 `objects` (the track object collisions, 0x45e2b0), bit 0x80 `walls` (the road edge walls, 0x45e2b0). The car keeps it as car+0x1d4 |
| 9 | **unk** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 10 | **polygon** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of the polygon in the high-res track chunk (`polygons_high_res_track`, chunk 4) of the block, which this record describes (nfs4.exe 0x439fe0) |
| 12 | **normal** | 6 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 15 bits is a fractional part | Normal vector of the polygon, unit 1/32768: the road frame on this polygon (nfs4.exe 0x439fe0, 0x4395f0) |
| 18 | **forward** | 6 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 15 bits is a fractional part | Forward vector of the polygon, unit 1/32768 (0x439fe0) |
### **Nfs4RefExtraObject** ###
#### **Size**: 20 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Reference to an extra object (XOBJ) placed in the track block: what the car collisions test (nfs4.exe 0x45d8c0) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **pt** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Position of the object |
| 12 | **radius** | 2 | 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Collision radius in meters, unit 1/256 m (nfs4.exe 0x439520 reads it as a signed 16-bit value, `<< 8` makes it 16.16), halved for `collision.type` 1 and doubled for 2. The object collision (0x45d8c0) uses the result: within the car radius + it, taller (2 x radius) than the car is above the ground |
| 14 | **global_index** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Sequence number of this object among all extra objects of the track: the index in the game's object state table (nfs4.exe 0x64f3c8, 512 entries of 3 bytes: standing / knocked away) |
| 16 | **unk1** | 3 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 19 | **collision** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>6-bits int "unk"<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: none<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: solid<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: knockable<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: crash_only | Collision byte. Bits 0..1 `type` (nfs4.exe 0x45d8c0, 0x437ed0): 0 none (skipped); 1 solid; 2 knockable: knocked away when the car (not AI) hits it at round(|vx| + |vz|) >= 11 m/s, played along CAN path 2 below 25 m/s, else 3 (a solid wall slower); 3 crash only: no response, a crash of 15 above 2 m/s. Type 1 also halves `radius`, 2 doubles it (0x439520). Other bits: unknown |

#### **Description**: Header of an extra object: type, position and the counts which define the sizes of the corresponding [Nfs4ExtraObject](#nfs4extraobject) arrays. nfs4.exe keeps the 0x34 bytes in place and writes the addresses of the object data into the pointer slots (0x4325f0) ####

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **type** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Object type. One of: 1, 2, 4 (normal static object), 3 (animated object, has `anim_data`), 6 (special/physics prop, has `special_data`). Objects of type 6 are placed in global chunks of the track file, not in track blocks: nfs4.exe makes rigid bodies of them (0x432e40, 0x431550; 306 in the NFS4 tracks, all in `global_objects_1`) |
| 4 | **index** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |

| 24 | **size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Size in bytes of the type data at the start of the object (`anim_data`: 8 + 20 x keyframes for type 3, `special_data`: 0x48 for type 6, 0 for the others): nfs4.exe 0x4325f0 reads that many bytes before the vertices |
| 28 | **data_pointer** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slot of the type data (0 when `size` is 0), written by the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4325f0); leftovers in the files |

| 36 | **vertex_pointers** | 8 | Array of `2` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slots of `vertices` and `vertex_shading`, written by the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4325f0); leftovers in the files |
| 44 | **num_polygons** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of polygons of the corresponding entry in `objects` |
| 48 | **polygons_pointer** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Run-time pointer slot of `polygons`, written by the loader (nfs4.exe 0x4325f0); leftovers in the files |

### **Nfs4HeightsSim** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Ceiling heights of the track slices (Data/Tracks/<track>/heights.sim, loaded by nfs4.exe 0x439c10): one float per `vroad` record of the FRD ([Nfs4VRoadBlock](#nfs4vroadblock)), the file is 4 bytes per slice in every NFS4 track. Without the file the game uses 10.0 for every slice ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **heights** | (file size / 4)\*4 | Array of `file size / 4` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: Float number (little-endian) | Ceiling height above the ground of each slice in meters, used where the car is covered (polygon surface bit 0x20, or side type 2 of its slice): a car higher than the slice centre + this hits the plane of the reversed road normal there (newton, nfs4.exe 0x4f5fd0). 3.27..25.96 in the NFS4 tracks |
### **Nfs4SpeedFile** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: AI line of the track (Data/Tracks/<track>/spdFA.bin forward, spdRA.bin reversed track; any case on disk), loaded by nfs4.exe 0x41c360 (0x41c4c0 picks the file): three arrays over the n track slices (`vroad` records of the FRD), the file is ceil(n / 2) + 5 n bytes in every NFS4 track. A shorter file is "Invalid speed file in track": the game then makes the AI line offsets itself from the (missing) lanes, 0x41c550 / 0x41e0d0; without the file it uses speed 64, lane 7 and offset 0. France also has a `spdB.bin` of the same layout that nfs4.exe does not load ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **speeds** | ceil(n / 2), n = 2 x file size // 11 | Array of `ceil(n / 2), n = 2 x file size // 11` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | AI target speed, one byte per two slices (slice s reads byte s / 2; nfs4.exe 0x41c500), in m/s by its uses (the AI and the unused driving aid 0x4fd580 compare it with the car speed; 0x41d3c0 keeps the track's highest). 17..119 in the NFS4 tracks (one 254 in Summit's spdRA) |
| ceil(n / 2), n = 2 x file size // 11 | **lanes** | n | Array of `n` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: Sub-byte compound block:<br/>4-bits int "lane"<br/>4-bits int "unk" | A byte per slice: the high 4 bits are the AI lane of the slice (nfs4.exe 0x41c550, 7 without the file; 1..10 in the NFS4 tracks), lanes numbered as in [Nfs4VRoadBlock](#nfs4vroadblock) (6 and 7 either side of the centre). When the file is short the game makes `line_offsets` from them (0x41e0d0: the lane centre, (lane - 6) x left lane width - width / 2 or (lane - 7) x right width + width / 2, kept 2 m inside the walls). The low 4 bits are 0 and not read |
| ceil(n / 2), n = 2 x file size // 11 + n | **line_offsets** | n\*4 | Array of `n` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: Float number (little-endian) | Lateral offset of the AI line from the slice centre in meters (along the `right` vector of the vroad record), a float per slice (nfs4.exe 0x41c590, 0 without the file): read by the AI cars and by the car reset when no lane of the slice is free (0x448c20) |
### **Nfs3CanAnimation** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Animation path (GameData/Tracks/TRK<nnn>/TR<nn><k>.CAN, TR<nn>00A.CAN). nfs3.exe plays them as the paths of knocked-away objects (TR<nn>00A.CAN as path 1, TR<nn>0<k>.CAN as path k + 1; the renderer 0x41ca40 -> 0x40f940 -> 0x40f4b0). NFS4 (Data/Tracks/<track>/Tr<nn>.can, any case) has the same files: nfs4.exe 0x41e760 loads `Tr00a.can` as path 0 and `Tr01.can` .. `Tr06.can` as paths 1..6 (`Tr00.can` is not loaded) and multiplies their positions by 1 / 1.3 (rounded to 16.16 again); a knocked object (`collision.type` 2 of [Nfs4RefExtraObject](#nfs4refextraobject)) plays path 2 below 25 m/s, else path 3 (0x437ed0). The `.CAN` files of NFS2 and NFS2 SE (GAMEDATA/TRACKS/DATA) have the same layout (their use there is not verified) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **size** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | File size in bytes, 8 + 20 * `num_keyframes` in every NFS2, NFS2 SE, NFS3 and NFS4 file |
| 2 | **unk** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The same in the same file of every NFS3 track (01: 0x0164, 02: 0x828e, 03: 0x8357, 04, 05: 0x8320, 06: 0x0269, 00A: 0 but TR0200A 0x41), other values in the 00 files; the same values in the NFS4 files (00A: 0 or 0x41) |
| 4 | **num_keyframes** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of keyframes |
| 6 | **ticks_per_frame** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Game ticks per keyframe; the game uses 6 when it is 0 or above 400. 6 in every file |
| 8 | **keyframes** | num_keyframes\*20 | Array of `num_keyframes` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs3CanKeyframe](#nfs3cankeyframe) | Keyframes |
### **Nfs3CanKeyframe** ###
#### **Size**: 20 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A keyframe of a CAN animation path, 20 bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Position in meters (16.16) |
| 12 | **orientation** | 8 | Rotation quaternion (x,y,z,w), in the same axes as the positions next to it, where each component is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 14 bits is a fractional part | Orientation quaternion, signed 16-bit values read as `(v << 2) / 65536` (unit 1/16384); unit length in every keyframe of the NFS2, NFS2 SE, NFS3 and NFS4 files |
## **Physics** ##
### **Nfs4CarPhysics** ###
#### **Size**: ? bytes ####
#### **Description**: NFS4 car physics: `carp.txt` in `Data/Cars/<car>/car.viv` (and `traffic/<car>`, `traffic/pursuit/<car>`; `carp<n>.txt`, n = game setup car +0x18, instead in race type 4: 1..3 in 11 cars, their upgrade levels by their values), plain text with CRLF line endings: pairs of a label line (`mass [kg](2)`) and a value line (`1275.000000`, arrays comma separated). nfs4.exe parses it with 0x503480 (car load 0x445090 -> 0x444fd0) into the car's carp (0x464 bytes): lines are read without spaces and lower-cased (0x5031f0, empty lines skipped, the file's last byte never read); a line containing the `(n)` of a field of the table 0x5bd414 (the first of the table, 0x503160; no key text is compared, unlike NFS3) is a label and the next line is always its value line, whatever it holds; other lines are skipped. Values are separated by `,` or tabs, read with `sscanf` ("%d" for integer fields, "%f" for floats, 0x502f40 / 0x503040); a value that is not a number ends the line, items a line lacks keep what the carp held (TailsLab: the default); a field given twice takes the later values. Fields missing from the file get the default carp 0x5be344 (Carp_FillDefaults 0x5032b0, `car_class` from 0x5bdee0). 81 fields, NFS3's 80 plus `understeer_gradient` (80); the torque curve has 21 points 500 rpm apart. Then Carp_TuneCar 0x4fcad0 applies the automatic gear set and the menus' tuning sliders, and sets the per gear values and the air drag. Car physics steps run at 32 Hz (every 2nd tick of the 64 Hz simulation). Field descriptions: label, place in the game's carp, the default for a missing field, then the use, from the nfs4.exe port in nfs-web (`src/nfs4/nfs4-physics`); "no reader found" = no ported code reads it (AI, sound and drawing code is not ported) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (0) | **serial_number** | 1 line | Integer in text, read with `sscanf("%d")` (nfs4.exe 0x502f40): an optional sign and digits, the rest of the item ignored (`128.000000` reads 128) | `Serial Number(0)` (carp+0x000; missing: 0). Serial number of the car (0 to 42; 0 in the traffic cars). No reader found in the ported nfs4.exe code |
| (1) | **car_class** | 1 line | Integer in text, read with `sscanf("%d")` (nfs4.exe 0x502f40): an optional sign and digits, the rest of the item ignored (`128.000000` reads 128) | `Car Classification(1)` (carp+0x004; missing: 0). Car class (0 to 3). No reader found in the ported nfs4.exe code. Missing: 0, from the second default image 0x5bdee0 (Carp_FillDefaults 0x5032b0 takes this field from it) |
| (2) | **mass** | 1 line | Decimal number in text, e.g. `1275.000000` (the shipped files write 6 decimals), read with `sscanf("%f")` into a float (nfs4.exe 0x503040) | `mass [kg](2)` (carp+0x008; missing: 1000). Mass in kg (915 to 9400). Drive acceleration of gear g (Carp_TuneCar 0x4fcad0) = velocity_to_rpm_ratio[g] / mass x 0.1 x gear_efficiency[g], in m/s² per N·m of torque. The body (Car_Reset 0x4448d0, body setup 0x4f4a20) gets this mass, x 3 for human players with the heavy cars option, x 1.1 as a cop player in single player games, / 1.0 (0x676118) for racers |
| (3) | **num_gears** | 1 line | Integer in text, read with `sscanf("%d")` (nfs4.exe 0x502f40): an optional sign and digits, the rest of the item ignored (`128.000000` reads 128) | `number of gears (reverse + neutral + forward gears)(3)` (carp+0x00c; missing: 8). Number of gears of the manual gearbox: reverse + neutral + forward (6 to 8; the gear tables have 8 entries: gear 0 reverse, 1 neutral, 2.. forward); gear num_gears - 1 is the top gear. Engine tuning slider t: entry i += (t - 1) x -0.1 x entry x (lo - i) / (hi - lo), lo = (redline + min rpm) / 2 / 500 + 3, hi = redline / 500 + 3 (the curve tilts about lo); game setup flag 1: x 1.75 |

The engine (0x4ffa20): rpm capped at it (above it by a third the wheels lock), rpm target = redline x throttle, engine cut while the rpm is above the wheels' rpm by more than redline / 6 in gears up to 3rd; with the gas off above 1.15 x the gear's speed at the redline the force scales down and the wheels lock. Carp_TuneCar (0x4fcad0) sets the air drag coefficient so that the drag (coefficient x speed³ x aero factor) is 0.98 x the top gear's drive at efficiency 1 (torque entry trunc(round(this x top gear ratio) / 500)) at this speed; above it the drag gets + 0.01 x (speed - this)² (0x4ffa20), the drag also x (1 + aero damage / 2). Tuning: engine slider t x (1 + (t - 1) x 0.1), gear ratio slider / t, aero slider / (1 + (t - 1) x 0.05); game setup flag 1: x 1.75 |

## **Images** ##
### **EacImage** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>64 (0x40): 4Bit PS1<br/>96 (0x60): DXT1 compressed bitmap<br/>97 (0x61): DXT3 compressed bitmap<br/>98 (0x62): DXT5 compressed bitmap<br/>109 (0x6d): 16Bit_4444 color format bitmap<br/>120 (0x78): 16Bit_0565 color format bitmap<br/>121 (0x79): 4Bit (swapped)<br/>122 (0x7a): 4Bit<br/>123 (0x7b): 8Bit<br/>125 (0x7d): 32Bit color format bitmap<br/>126 (0x7e): 16Bit_1555 color format bitmap<br/>127 (0x7f): 24Bit color format bitmap</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of the image to the first block attached to it: the palette of an 8Bit image, hot spots (0x7C), text (0x6F), and in NFS6 0x69 / 0x70 blocks. Every attached block starts with its id and the offset to the next one (0 in the last), so they make a chain, which this parser follows. 0 when nothing is attached (then an 8Bit image uses !pal or !PAL of the SHPI), never the size of the image block. Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field is attached. TNFS has other values in a few car (CFM) and track (FAM) textures without attached blocks: mostly a negative offset to the !PAL item of the SHPI, sometimes garbage |
| 4 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap width in pixels |
| 6 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap height in pixels |
| 8 | **pivot** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | TNFS dashboards add both coordinates to the points of `hot_spots`. y coordinate is used by the horizon bitmap "horz" of TNFS FAM files when the game scrolls it (horizon "ring type" 0, the open road tracks by default): this row of the bitmap lies on the horizon line (Win95 SE FUN_0043ae64). The horizon ring (ring type 1, the closed tracks) does not use it |
| 12 | **position** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap position on screen. Used for menu/dash sprites. In NFS5 FSH files this is the position of the image in a texture page (atlas), which is used by CRP models: 12 lower bits of each coordinate are a signed value, 4 higher bits of y are the amount of `mipmaps` levels (always all of them down to 1x1, 0 without mipmaps), set on save |
| 16 | **bitmap** | width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Bytes | Pixel color table. For 8Bit bitmap each value represents an index of color in the attached palette. Palette can be stored: <br/>- right after 8Bit image<br/>- as !pal/!PAL in the same SHPI<br/>- in a different SHPI before this one (if it is WWWW archive)<br/>- even in different QFS file (TNFS, CONTROL directory).<br/>Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md). DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 bitmaps are S3TC-compressed 4x4 pixel blocks (8, 16 and 16 bytes per block) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **mipmaps** | 0..(1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Optional (if dimensions are powers of two and position.y has the amount of levels): Bytes | Mipmaps pixel data in the same format as `bitmap` field. There are images with sizes w/2 x h/2, w/4 x h/4, .... up to 1x1, in descending order, each padded with zeros to 16 bytes. Only NFS5 files have them: the 4 high bits of `position.y` hold the amount of levels |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **pad** | 0..up to offset next_offset | Optional (if next_offset points past the pixels): Padding bytes | Bytes between the pixels (and mipmaps) and the first attached block: zeros, or leftovers aligning it |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness + up to offset next_offset | **embedded_palette** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has a palette here): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | Embedded palette, which should be assigned to this bitmap (except for ga00 in TR2_001.FAM) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the embedded palette and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x7C here): [ShpiHotSpots](#shpihotspots) | Hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap, read by TNFS dashboards |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the hot spots and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **text** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x6F here): [ShpiText](#shpitext) | Shpi text |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_2** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | A palette after the last attached block, which no block links to (some textures of TNFS TR* tracks) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_3** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_4** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
### **EacPalette** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Resource with colors LUT (look-up table). EA 8-bit bitmaps have 1-byte value per pixel, meaning the index of color in LUT of assigned palette. Has special colors: 255th in most cases means transparent color, 254th in TNFS car textures is replaced by tail light color, 250th - 253th are the cop car light bar (TNFS maps them to the VGA palette entries 0xFA - 0xFD: red, dark red, blue, dark blue, swapped every 16 clock ticks during a police chase, Win95 SE `gfx_draw_car_model` 0x458d4c) and are rendered black in other cars. The converter writes these colors to `car_colors.json` next to the PNGs.<br/>TNFS car models (CFM) have a second palette `!xxx` next to `!PAL` in the high-poly textures SHPI (TRAFFC in both): the car's slice of the shared 256-color VGA palette in 8-bit modes (Win95 SE `gfx_car_palettes_setup` 0x4572e0). Its first 23 colors (8 for traffic, 24 for the player in a single race / tournament) go to the car's palette entries (player 0x30, opponent 0x48, traffic 0x60 + 8 * slot), then the textures are remapped from `!PAL` to the nearest colors of the VGA palette. `!PAL` is the palette of the textures, `!xxx` is never used to draw them. Cops get none, and the `M*.CFM` models (opponents of a single race / tournament, which share `CARFAMS/CARPAL.FSH` instead) have junk there. Many `!xxx` have the 8-bit bitmap id 0x7B (256x1 or 256x3) instead of a palette id. The converter writes its used colors to `car_colors.json` (`palette_slice`) instead of a file of its own ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>34 (0x22): 24BitDos color format palette<br/>36 (0x24): 24Bit color format palette<br/>41 (0x29): 16Bit_0565 color format palette<br/>42 (0x2a): 32Bit color format palette<br/>45 (0x2d): 16Bit_1555 color format palette</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | When attached to a bitmap: offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows. 0 in palette items (`!pal`) |
| 4 | **num_colors** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of colors |
| 6 | **unk1** | 2 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **num_colors1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Equals to num_colors, except for some CRP structures in NFS5 |
| 10 | **unk2** | 6 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 16 | **colors** | ? | Type according to enum `resource_id`:<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Colors LUT. Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md) |
### **ShpiHotSpots** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A list of hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap it is attached to (after the bitmap and its embedded palette), the index of a point gives its meaning. Many bitmaps of menus, track (FAM) and car (CFM) textures have an empty list, others in the same files have none, and 1x1 placeholder bitmaps of dashboards have copies of the list of another bitmap. TNFS reads it in the dashboard loader only (DOS `tnfs_dash_000522be`, Win95 SE FUN_0041f9a0, the demo `tnfs_dashboard_load`; PSX and 3DO do not read FSH dashboards), from four bitmaps of `SIMDATA/DASH/*DH.FSH` / `*DL.FSH`:<br/>- `dash`: 10 points. 0, 1 = top left and bottom right corners of the rear-view mirror; 2 = radar detector power light; 3..7 = the 5 radar detector level lights; 8, 9 = the loader turns them into offsets from 2 and 3, nothing reads them<br/>- `tach`: tachometer needle tip at 0, 1024, 2048... RPM (the needle is interpolated between them), the last point is the needle centre<br/>- `sped`: speedometer needle tip at 0, 10, 20... mph (0, 20, 40... km/h in the German version), the last point is the needle centre. The cars with a digital speedometer draw digits instead<br/>- `gate`: gear lever knob position for every gear: 0 = reverse, 1 = neutral, then gears from 1st: 7 or 8 points. The game reads 9 points (a 9th, where present, is at the corner of the bitmap)<br/>The game walks the attached blocks until it finds 0x7C, so it hangs when one of these bitmaps has no hot spots ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x7c | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **num_points** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of points array |
| 8 | **points** | num_points\*8 | Array of `num_points` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Points in screen pixels, relative to the bitmap: the screen point is `position` + `pivot` + point, so `pivot` + point is the pixel of the bitmap. TNFS reads the low byte of the amount only |
### **ShpiText** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Text attached to an SHPI image. In the NFS3 / NFS4 sky archives (`SKY.FSH`, `sky.qfs`) the `SUN*` images carry the sun sprite settings: the numbers after `A` (azimuth, degrees), `B` and `R` (the sprite's corners are 10 * R from its centre) and the words `ROTATE`, `NOADD` (not additive), `INFRONT` (drawn after the clouds) (nfs3.exe 0x47a970, nfs4.exe 0x4c9050, which reads it only when `Tr.ini` has no `hasSun=1`). Elsewhere the purpose is unclear ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x6f | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **len_text** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of 'text' utf8 block |
| 8 | **text** | len_text | UTF-8 string | Text contents |
## **Fonts** ##
### **FfnFont** ###
#### **Size**: 48..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Bitmap font: a font atlas bitmap plus glyph definitions (position and size of each symbol in the atlas) and optional kerning table ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. One of ['"FNTF"', '"FNTP"', '"FNTS"', '"FNTX"', '"FNTM"', '"FNTG"', '"FNTA"', '"FntF"', '"FntP"', '"FntS"', '"FntX"', '"FntM"', '"FntG"', '"FntA"'] | Resource ID |
| 4 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this FFN block in bytes. Does not include the embedded palette of an 8Bit bitmap (and padding to it after bitmap data); the palette of a 4Bit bitmap (NFS6) is included. For older versions (I set version <= 101, but it can be anywhere up to < 309), "padding_2" length not included as well |
| 8 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Font format version. Defines the layout of glyph definitions (see [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition)): 11 bytes below 200, 12 bytes up to 309 (last one padding), 12 bytes with `num_kern` above 309, 16 bytes from 321 with the `format` flag 16-bytes. Changing it changes the size of every glyph definition. Game fonts: 100 / 101 (TNFS to NFS4), 309 to 366 (NFS6) |
| 10 | **num_glyphs** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of symbols, defined in this font |
| 12 | **flags** | 4 | Sub-byte compound block (little endian):<br/>13-bits int "pad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: 12-bytes<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: 16-bytes<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: ASCII<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Unicode<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Shift-JIS<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Reserved<br/>4-bits int "layoutpad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: LTR<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: RTL<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Horizontal<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Vertical<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Roman (english)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Ideographic (Kanji)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Hanging (Arabic)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Unknown<br/>4-bits int "drawpad"<br/>1-bit flag "vram"<br/>1-bit flag "outline"<br/>1-bit flag "dropshadow"<br/>1-bit flag "antialiased" | Font flags: format of glyph definitions, encoding, layout and draw attributes |
| 16 | **center** | 2 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 18 | **ascent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the top of the glyphs in pixels. `ascent + descent` is the line height, and a glyph is drawn `y_offset` below the top of its line. NFS6 capitals end at `ascent`; TNFS and NFS2 fonts have `descent` 0 and keep the whole line height here |
| 19 | **descent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the bottom of the glyphs in pixels: NFS6 descenders end at `ascent + descent` |
| 20 | **definitions_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to definitions block |
| 24 | **kernings_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to kernings. 0 if there is no kernings table |
| 28 | **bdata_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to bitmap block |
| 32 | **padding_0** | up to offset definitions_ptr | Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| definitions_ptr | **definitions** | num_glyphs\*11..num_glyphs\*17 | Array of `num_glyphs` items<br/>Item type: [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition) | Definitions of chars in this bitmap font, sorted by `code` (the writer keeps this order, stable sort by `code`) |
| ? | **padding_1** | 0..up to offset kernings_ptr | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| ? | **kernings** | 0..? | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Array, prefixed with length field<br/>Length field type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>Item type: [KerningItem](#kerningitem) | Kerning pairs table. For versions > 309 (glyphs with `num_kern`) the pairs are sorted by right glyph, so the pairs of one right glyph follow each other: the writer keeps this order (stable sort by `right`) |
| ? | **padding_2** | up to offset bdata_ptr | Padding bytes | Puts the bitmap at the offset the game files use: versions < 309 at a multiple of 16 (gap filled with 0xAD; NFS2 SWISS36 at a multiple of 8), newer ones so that the pixels after the 16-byte bitmap header start at a multiple of 128 (gap starts with "Buy ERTS", then zeros). Recomputed on save when the glyph or kerning tables change size, keeping the alignment of the file read |
| bdata_ptr | **bitmap** | 16..? | [EacImage](#eacimage) | Font atlas bitmap data |
| ? | **remaining_bytes** | remaining bytes | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
### **GlyphDefinition** ###
#### **Size**: 11..17 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Glyph definition.<br/>- for FNT version < 200 has length 11 bytes.<br/>- for versions >= 200 and <= 309 - 12 bytes, last byte is padding.<br/>- for versions > 309 - 12th byte is num_kern.<br/>- for versions >= 321 it may be 16 bytes if "format" flag is set to 16-bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **code** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of symbol |
| 2 | **width** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Width of symbol in font bitmap |
| 3 | **height** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Height of symbol in font bitmap |
| 4 | **x** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (x) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 6 | **y** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (y) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 8 | **advance** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text. 0 in every game font with 16-byte glyphs, which keep it in `x_advance` |
| 9 | **x_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (x) for drawing the character image |
| 10 | **y_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (y) for drawing the character image |
| 11 | **num_kern** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version > 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Number of kerning pairs with this glyph as the right (second) glyph |
| 11..12 | **pad** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version <= 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Padding |
| 11..13 | **kern_index** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the first kerning pair with this glyph as the right glyph: its `num_kern` pairs follow each other in the kerning table from here. 0 if the glyph has no kerning pairs |
| 11..15 | **x_advance** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text, for 16-byte glyphs (`advance` is 0 in all of them in the game files) |
### **KerningItem** ###
#### **Size**: 4 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Kerning pair: horizontal adjustment of the gap between two specific glyphs ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **left** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of left glyph |
| 2 | **kerning** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Kerning amount in pixels, added to the gap between the glyphs |
| 3 | **right** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Code of right glyph |
## **Audio** ##
### **EaAudioStreams** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A file of EA audio streams (`SCHl`): NFS2 / NFS2 SE `.ASF` (a song), NFS2 / NFS2 SE / NFS3 `.MUS` (interactive music: a stream per node of the `.MAP` file of the same name), NFS4 `Data/Audio/MUSIC/*.ASF`, NFS5 songs in `GameData/Music/zzzymus.viv`, NFS6 `audio/music/*.asf`, NFS6 speech in `radio.viv`. Converted to WAV with FFmpeg: a file with one stream to `<name>.wav` + `<name>.meta.json` (loop), a file with more streams to a folder with `<index>.wav` + `<index>.meta.json` per stream and `playthrough.wav` (the streams in the order of the `.LIN`, else `.MAP` file next to it, see `EaMusicMap`; all streams in file order without one) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **streams** | streams up to the end of file\*12..? | Array of `streams up to the end of file` items<br/>Item type: [EaAudioStream](#eaaudiostream) | Audio streams |
### **EaAudioStream** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA audio stream (NFS2 - NFS6 music, NFS6 speech): header chunk "SCHl" with a sound patch (sampling rate, channels, number of samples, loop, codec), then the wave data in chunks of 8-byte header (id, length including the header) and data: SCCl (amount of SCDl chunks), SCDl (wave data), SCLl (loop end), SCEl (end). Explained by [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`); the converter decodes it with FFmpeg ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SCHl" | Header chunk id |
| 4 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of the header chunk, including the chunk id and this field |
| 8 | **header** | 4..? | [EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch) | Sound patch: tags before `info_start` are playback settings, the ones after it describe the wave data. Without the `version` tag (NFS2 - NFS4) `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, no `codec` is 16-bit little endian PCM (NFS3 menu music: each SCDl chunk holds the amount of samples, 4 bytes, then the samples, channels interleaved), the sampling rate is 22050 without `sampling_rate`; with `version` 1 (NFS5, NFS6) the codec is EA-XA ADPCM v2 ("R1" in FFmpeg). `loop_start` / `loop_end` are sample indices of the loop |
| 12..? | **header_padding** | header_length - (header fields length) | Bytes | Zeros up to the end of the header chunk |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length)..? | **data** | chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl | Bytes | Chunks SCCl, SCDl, SCLl, SCEl with the wave data, as they are in the file |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length) + chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl..? | **padding** | up to the next stream or the end of file | Bytes | Zeros aligning the next stream of the file to 4 bytes |
### **EaSoundPatch** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound patch ("PT" header): a sound of a BNKl sound bank as a list of tags. Tags before `info_start` are playback settings (priority, volume, pan, pitch bend range...), tags after it describe the wave data: `num_samples`, `channels` (default 1), `sampling_rate` (default 22050), loop sample indices `loop_start` and `loop_end` (inclusive; a sample loops when it has one of them, from 0 / up to the last sample when the other one is missing), `data_offset` (wave data offset from the start of the bank file) and the codec. Without the `version` tag, `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, 9 is EA MicroTalk 10:1 (speech), no `codec` tag is 16-bit little endian PCM. With `version` 1, `codec_2` 8 is 16-bit little endian PCM, 9 is signed 8-bit PCM, no `codec_2` tag is EA-XA ADPCM v2. Stereo samples are interleaved. A sound can have several layers, played together, separated by the `layer_end` tag, each one with its own settings and wave data (NFS3 player car engines add a short mono loop to the stereo engine sample) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **platform_magic** | 2 | UTF-8 string. Always == "PT" | Patch header magic |
| 2 | **platform** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Platform id, 0 is PC |
| 4 | **tags** | up to and including tag "end"..? | Array of `up to and including tag "end"` items<br/>Item type: [EaSoundPatchTag](#easoundpatchtag) | Tags |
### **EaSoundPatchTag** ###
#### **Size**: 1..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A tag of EA sound patch: tag id, then (except for tags 0xFC-0xFF) the length of the value and the value, big endian unsigned. Tag meanings follow [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`), the ones named `unk_*` are not known ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **tag** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>0 (0x0): unk_0x00<br/>6 (0x6): priority<br/>7 (0x7): unk_0x07<br/>8 (0x8): release_envelope<br/>9 (0x9): playback_envelope<br/>10 (0xa): bend_range_semitones<br/>11 (0xb): bank_channels<br/>12 (0xc): pan<br/>13 (0xd): random_pan_range<br/>14 (0xe): volume<br/>15 (0xf): random_volume_range<br/>16 (0x10): detune<br/>17 (0x11): random_detune_range<br/>18 (0x12): unk_0x12<br/>19 (0x13): effect_bus<br/>20 (0x14): user_data<br/>128 (0x80): version<br/>130 (0x82): channels<br/>131 (0x83): codec<br/>132 (0x84): sampling_rate<br/>133 (0x85): num_samples<br/>134 (0x86): loop_start<br/>135 (0x87): loop_end<br/>136 (0x88): data_offset<br/>137 (0x89): data_offset_channel_2<br/>138 (0x8a): unk_0x8a<br/>139 (0x8b): unk_0x8b<br/>140 (0x8c): flags<br/>145 (0x91): unk_0x91<br/>146 (0x92): unk_0x92<br/>147 (0x93): unk_0x93<br/>160 (0xa0): codec_2<br/>252 (0xfc): padding<br/>253 (0xfd): info_start<br/>254 (0xfe): layer_end<br/>255 (0xff): end</details> | Tag id |
| 1 | **value_length** | 0..1 | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): 1-byte unsigned integer | Length of value in bytes. 0 means value 0 |
| 1..2 | **value** | 0..value_length | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): Bytes | Value, big endian unsigned integer |
## **Misc** ##
### **Nfs4TrackIni** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Track settings of NFS4, `Data/Tracks/<track>/Tr.ini` (day; `TrN.ini` night, `TrW.ini` weather, `TrNW.ini` night with weather), a Windows INI file read by nfs4.exe 0x4c70a0 with `GetPrivateProfileString`. Sky sections: `[strip]` the horizon band (`hrzShouldDrawBlack`, `hrzMirror`, `hrzHasPMX`, `hrzBottomYOff` base y relative to the eye, `hrzGouraudHeight`, `hrzGouraudMiddle`, `hrzPmxTop`, `hrzPmxBottom` offsets from the base, colours `[r,g,b]` `hrzSunColor`, `hrzOppositeSunColor`, `hrzEarthTopColor`, `hrzEarthBotColor`, `hrzSkyTopColor`, `hrzfRadius` and `hrzAngle` in turns: NFS3 `3TR<nn>.HRZ` values under names, the strips are `HDC0`..`HDC7` of `sky.qfs`); `[clouds]` (`cloudType` 0 none, 1 additive, 2 blend; `cloudBright`, `cloudVariance`, `cloudNimbus` 0..1, `cloudFog`, `cloudVisualHeight`, `windSpeed`, `windDir`, `cloudYOffset`, `cloudHeight` (NFS3's dome height already multiplied by 3), `cloudUscale` / `cloudVscale` texture repeats per grid cell); `[fog]` (`fogColor`, `fogDensity`, `fogHorizon`, `fogNumRegions`, regions in `[fog region <n>]`); `[sun]` (`hasSun`, `angleTheta` azimuth and `angleRho` in turns: direction (cos theta, cos rho, sin theta), `radius` of the sprite, `rotates`, `additive`, `inFront` drawn after the clouds). Other sections: `[lightning]`, `[weather]`, `[light]`, `[special]`, `[track glows]`. See `library/utils/eac_horizon_to_spherical.py` ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **text** | the whole file | UTF-8 string | The INI text |
